title: Methods
description: Instance methods, self, and special methods

exercises.title: Define a Method
exercises.description: Define a method on a struct type 'Person' with a 'Name' field that returns a greeting string.
exercises.starter_code: record Person(string Name) { public string Greet() => "Hello, " + Name; }
hints: Instance methods attach to structs/classes with implicit `this`.
Return interpolated greetings built from encapsulated state.

exercises.title: Pointer Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a pointer receiver that modifies the receiver's state. Create a 'SetName' method on Person.
exercises.starter_code: class Person { public string Name = "Bob"; public void SetName(string n) => Name = n; }
hints: Mutators on reference types (`class`) change shared heap state instantly.
Public instance methods idiomatically use PascalCase identifiers.

exercises.title: Value Receiver
exercises.description: Define a method with a value receiver that returns a new value without modifying the original.
exercises.starter_code: record Counter(int Value) { public Counter Increment() => this with { Value = Value + 1 }; }
hints: `record` types support `with` expressions for immutable-friendly updates.
Value receivers/`readonly` structs communicate non-mutating APIs.

exercises.title: Interface Satisfaction
exercises.description: Define a 'Stringer' interface with a String() method, then satisfy it with a type.
exercises.starter_code: record Point(int X, int Y) { public override string ToString() => $"Point({X}, {Y})"; }
hints: Override `ToString()` to satisfy customary `.NET` stringification hooks.
Alternatively implement `IFormattable` if richer formatting emerges later.
exercises.solution:
Console.WriteLine(new Point(10, 20));

record Point(int X, int Y) { public override string ToString() => $"Point({X}, {Y})"; }

exercises.title: Method Chaining
exercises.description: Define a Builder type with Methods Add(str) Builder and Build() string. Add returns the Builder for chaining. Test by chaining Add("Hello").Add("World").Build().
exercises.starter_code: class Builder { public string Result = ""; public Builder Add(string s) { Result += s; return this; } public string Build() => Result; }
hints: Fluent builders return `this` from mutators enabling chained calls.
Accumulate into internal buffers before exposing `.Build()`.

exercises.title: Multiple Methods on Same Type
exercises.description: Define a Circle type with Radius double. Add two methods: Area() double and Perimeter() double. Create a circle with radius 5.0, compute both, and Console.WriteLine them.
exercises.starter_code: record Circle(double Radius) { public double Area() => Math.PI * Radius * Radius; public double Perimeter() => 2 * Math.PI * Radius; }
hints: Share `Math.PI` between perimeter/area calculations on the same radius.
High-precision textual output aligns with invariant `G17`/`R` formatter needs.

exercises.title: Method on Primitive Type
exercises.description: Create a type MyInt int. Define a method IsEven() bool on MyInt that returns true if the value is even. Test with MyInt(42).
exercises.starter_code: readonly struct MyInt(int Value) { public bool IsEven() => Value % 2 == 0; }
hints: Wrap primitives with `struct MyInt` or `readonly struct` for semantic safety.
Boolean emission may require `.ToLowerInvariant()` for lowercase expectations.
